bustouts: Oh Babe, It Ain't No Lie

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Oh Babe, It Ain't No Lie** (3 reviews): A taper friend who attended says Weir was not onstage for this song; Jerry unexpectedly played this song; the reviewer was delighted [13][15][18]
- **CC Rider** (1 review): Reviewer calls it a top-tier version, part of a first set that rocks throughout [18]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Reviewer hears it as a train wreck in an otherwise okay performance [17]
- **Don't Need Love** (1 review): Reviewer says this was its first-ever performance, and reads that Jerry and Phil had left the stage [19]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): This early rendition lets you hear how the song began [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Oh Babe, It Ain't No Lie**: back after 154 archived shows (894 days) [24]
- **Cihna Cat Sunflower**: rare: 11 archived performances [24]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Don't Need Love [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-03-28.148338.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1984-03-28.177915.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 163 min [2]
- **gd1984-03-28.170203.akg.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 157 min [4]
- **gd1984-03-28.176070.neumann.km84i.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 153 min [6]
- **gd84-03-28.fob-faintych.miller.27303.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 3.44/5 by 16 [10]. Said about its sound: Audience is cut out between first-set songs, and Drums is mostly missing from the second set; Nice recording with good presence and noticeable audience participation [17][22]

## Around the show

- This was the first show of 1984 and the opener of a four-show run [14]
- The shows were Rex Foundation benefits with $25 tickets, roughly twice the usual price; band members chatted with fans in the parking lot afterward [14]
- Jerry mentioned guitar trouble from the stage and the crowd cheered [15]
- Weir's amp had technical problems at the start of set two, so the band opened with an electric Oh Babe without him [2]
- Weir's amp trouble at the second set's start led to an electric Oh Babe, It Ain't No Lie without him [4]
- Weir's amp problems at the start of set two meant an electric Oh Babe opener without him [6]
- Even by 1984 standards, this was by far the smallest hall the band played, and in their hometown [14]
- Reviewer ranks the 3/28 to 4/1 Marin run among the hottest, alongside the spring 1984 Hult Center shows [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-03-28.148338.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [1]. Also: Short patches in Don't Need Love and Drums come from a Beyer M160/Sennheiser 421 source, shnid 109259; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction [1]
- **gd1984-03-28.177915.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [2]
- **gd1984-03-28.170203.akg.clugston.flac1644**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Audience Cassettes; AKG mics (unknown model) > DAT (16/44) [4]. Also: The AKG d330bt and Sennheiser 421 blend from Chris Hecht and Charlie Miller supplies the first 1:21 of Iko Iko; The same blend source supplies a short patch in the Playin' In The Band to Don't Need Love transition [4]
- **gd1984-03-28.176070.neumann.km84i.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bill Bradt; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bill Bradt's Master Audience Cassettes: Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: AKG d330bt/Sennheiser 421 blend supplies patches after Don't Need Love and in the Drums to Space transition [6]
- **gd84-03-28.fob-faintych.miller.27303.sbeok.shnf**: source: (FOB/20th Row) Sony ECM 939LT> Cassette Master (Marantz PMD430) [10]
